meta_description:
6,126 likes, 30 comments - cntraveler on October 30, 2026: "You're in for a spooky trip that goes beyond your average ghost tour in New Orleans, Louisiana, known for its spiritual history, centuries-old cemeteries, French Quarter legends, and NOLA Halloween spirit, captured here by @nocturnalnola.

Commerce writer @jeschapel knows the best way to do it, starting with the city's roots in voodoo: a spiritual tradition shaped by West African practices, Catholicism, and the Haitian diaspora. You can dig into the history of Marie Laveau—the legendary 19th-century voodoo practitioner whose name still pops up all over the city—at @mlhouseofvoodoo in the French Quarter. Or you can take an expert-led voodoo tour, where you'll learn all about the history and how it's ingrained in the city's culture today. @voodoomuseum can also help put the traditions into context.

Be sure to also make your way to the Garden District to visit Buckner Mansion, the enormous Greek Revival house built in 1857 that American Horror Story: Coven fans will recognize as Miss Robichaux’s Academy. (It’s a private home, so you'll have to admire it from the sidewalk rather than tour inside.) You can also check into the @hotelmonteleone, a French Quarter landmark dating back to 1886 with generations of reported ghost stories, from doors said to open on their own to mysterious elevator stops. I stayed there myself and found no sign of ghosts—they do make a terribly mean martini in the lobby bar, though.

For even more Halloween spirit, attend a witch brunch at @coppervine, reserve your spot at the Endless Night Vampire Ball at the @hobnola, take an adults-only ghost tour, or visit haunted houses like @themortuary or @neworleansnightmare_.".
